items.title: Justin Timberlake to Release Four-Part ‘Tell-All’ Docuseries, Featuring Janet Jackson, on Apple (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary:
Justin Timberlake has a four-part documentary series heading to Apple TV in December, with Janet Jackson appearing to discuss the 2004 Super Bowl halftime performance that ended with the so-called wardrobe malfunction. Variety reported the project, citing three sources who confirmed the series and described it as a tell-all. Fisher Stevens is directing.

One source told Variety that Timberlake also addresses recent comments made by his former girlfriend Britney Spears. Representatives for Timberlake, Jackson and Apple either declined to comment or did not respond to the outlet's requests. Further details on the series, including an exact release date, were not available.

Timberlake's ties to Apple go back to 2021, when he starred in the Apple Original film Palmer. The docuseries arrives after a quiet stretch for the singer, who turned up as a guest during Jay-Z's concert in Paris last month but has largely stayed out of view since wrapping his Forget Tomorrow world tour in July 2025.

That tour, in support of Everything I Thought It Was, released in March 2024, ran into complications. Timberlake announced in July 2025 that he had been diagnosed with Lyme disease, which he said accounted for the nerve damage and fatigue fans noticed during low-energy performances on the international leg. "I've been battling some health issues, and was diagnosed with Lyme Disease–which I don't say so you feel bad for me – but to shed some light on what I've been up against behind the scenes," he wrote.

The tour also followed his DWI conviction stemming from a June 2024 arrest in Sag Harbor, New York, after police pulled him over for running a stop sign and drifting out of his lane. Page Six reported at the time that he told officers the incident would ruin the tour, but bodycam footage released later indicated he said something closer to "I'm on tour." The docuseries is set to land in December.

items.title: Netflix Orders ‘Prep’ YA Series Based On Book From ‘One Day’ EP Nicole Taylor & Gloria Sanchez Prods.
items.summary:
Netflix has handed a straight-to-series order to Prep, a half-hour adaptation of Curtis Sittenfeld's 2005 debut novel. Nicole Taylor, the head writer and executive producer of Netflix's limited series One Day, writes and showruns, with Gloria Sanchez Productions producing. Deadline reported the order, noting the project had been developed internally at the streamer.

Sittenfeld's novel follows Lee Fiora, a scholarship student navigating four years at Ault, an elite New England boarding school, and the friendships, crushes and class anxieties that come with being an outsider among wealthy classmates. Taylor executive produces alongside Will Ferrell, Jessica Elbaum and Alix Taylor for Gloria Sanchez, with Sittenfeld also executive producing. A writers room opens in January.

The green light arrives nearly 22 years after Random House published the book, and a decade after HBO developed it as a comedy series from Colleen McGuinness and Carolyn Strauss, a version that never moved forward. Netflix's take uses the half-hour format but is not a comedy, following the pattern of One Day, whose episodes ran between 19 and 38 minutes.

"Prep is my all time favourite novel and I have longed to adapt it for the entire twenty years since I first read it and found myself reflected uncannily back," Taylor said, calling it the most truthful take on "the perils of social mobility." Sittenfeld said the wait was worth it, adding, "Nicole's adaptation makes me understand my own novel, and myself, better."

Prep joins a young-adult slate at Netflix that includes The Sticks, The Body, Poser and Sid & Zoey. The streamer says YA titles have drawn more than 10.4 billion global views since it began publishing comprehensive viewership data in the first half of 2023, with Wednesday and Stranger Things accounting for four entries on its most popular English-language series list.

Taylor won a BAFTA TV Award for the BBC's three-part Three Girls and wrote the miniseries The Nest and the film Wild Rose, her stage adaptation of which opens off-Broadway this month. Sittenfeld's other novels include Romantic Comedy, in development as a film at New Line and Hello Sunshine, and Rodham, previously set up as a series at Hulu.

items.title: Steve Ellis Dies: “Everlasting Love” Singer Was 76
items.summary:
Steve Ellis, the singer who fronted the British pop group Love Affair and delivered the vocal on their 1967 hit "Everlasting Love," died October 30 from complications of a chronic illness. He was 76. His family announced the death on his Facebook page, saying he died peacefully with loved ones present at his home in Brighton, England, as Deadline reported.

"Everlasting Love" was a cover of a Robert Knight song, and Love Affair's version went to No. 1 in the UK while failing to chart in the United States. Carl Carlton's 1974 recording became the more familiar American version, later turning up in the 2000 film American Psycho and in trailers for Belfast in 2021, where Jamie Dornan sings it in the film itself.

The single also produced a controversy at home when it emerged that session musicians had played everything on the record except Ellis's vocal. The band's lineup otherwise consisted of keyboardist Lynton Guest, guitarist Rex Brayley, drummer Maurice Bacon and bassist Mick Jackson.

Love Affair followed with three more UK Top 10 singles across 1968 and 1969 — "Rainbow Valley," "A Day Without Love" and "Bringing on Back the Good Times" — while "One Road" reached the Top 20. Ellis left in 1969 for a solo career and kept recording and performing for decades, frequently alongside reassembled versions of the band.

Born Stephen John Ellis in Edgware, Middlesex, on April 7, 1950, he wrote on Facebook last year that he was pulling out of a planned tour. "I have never fully recovered from Covid in 2020 and chronic symptoms since have compromised my ability to sustain lengthy touring anymore," he said.
